research_question: In adults with heart disease, what is the effect of home-based cardiac rehabilitation (including digital/telehealth-supported programmes) compared with supervised centre-based cardiac rehabilitation on triglyceride levels (mmol/L) at 3–12 months follow-up?
treatment_label: Home-based cardiac rehabilitation (including telehealth/digital/mobile-supported home programmes)
outcome_description: Serum/plasma triglyceride concentration, expressed in mmol/L (values reported in mg/dL converted by dividing by 88.57). Arm-level mean, SD and N extracted at the latest eligible follow-up between 3 and 12 months; either absolute follow-up values or change-from-baseline values accepted, whichever the paper reports. Where only median with IQR/range is reported, mean and SD estimated using the methods of Wan et al. (2014). In multi-arm trials, each eligible home-based arm is compared separately against the shared supervised centre-based control arm.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges g means the home-based cardiac rehabilitation group had HIGHER triglyceride levels than the supervised centre-based group (i.e. a less favourable lipid outcome for home-based rehabilitation); a negative value favours home-based rehabilitation (lower triglycerides).
search_queries: home-based cardiac rehabilitation versus centre-based randomized trial lipids triglycerides
telerehabilitation cardiac rehabilitation randomised controlled trial coronary heart disease outcomes
telehealth home exercise programme cardiac patients trial cholesterol triglyceride effect
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trial in adults with heart disease (e.g. coronary artery disease, post-MI, post-revascularisation, heart failure, valve surgery)
Compares a home-based cardiac rehabilitation programme (including digital, telehealth, mobile or remotely supported home programmes) against a supervised centre-based cardiac rehabilitation programme
Reports some quantitative triglyceride data (mean/SD, median/IQR, or statistics convertible to an effect size) at a follow-up point between 3 and 12 months
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, opinion piece, commentary, theoretical/methodological paper, conference abstract without data, or study protocol)
Not a randomised controlled trial, or comparator is usual care, waitlist, no intervention, or any non-centre-based control rather than supervised centre-based cardiac rehabilitation
No quantitative triglyceride outcome data usable for an effect size (no means+SDs, medians+IQRs, t/F values, or other convertible statistics) at 3–12 months follow-up
Completely unrelated to cardiac rehabilitation in adults with heart disease, or reports only outcomes other than triglycerides
moderators_to_extract: Delivery modality of home-based arm (unsupervised home exercise vs telehealth/digital/mobile-supported)
Cardiac diagnosis / population (coronary artery disease or post-MI/PCI/CABG vs heart failure vs mixed)
Follow-up timepoint used (3–6 months vs >6–12 months)
Programme duration and intensity (weeks of intervention)
Outcome data type (absolute follow-up values vs change-from-baseline; measured vs estimated from median/IQR)
Sample size category and country/region of the trial
effect_size_note: Extract arm-level mean, SD and N for triglycerides in mmol/L (convert mg/dL to mmol/L by dividing by 88.57). Use the latest eligible follow-up between 3 and 12 months. Absolute follow-up values and change-from-baseline values are both acceptable and should not be a reason for exclusion; record which type was used. If only median and IQR/range are given, estimate mean and SD via Wan et al. (2014). For multi-arm trials, enter each home-based arm vs the shared centre-based control as a separate comparison, noting the shared control to allow for correlated-effects handling.
